title: MAG-S3: what a recording experiment needs to see the shape of the quantum compass
description: Simulation study of the recording experiment that could test the MAG-S2 prediction in birds: neurons that read a radical-pair (cryptochrome) magnetic compass carry a population code shaped like the real projective plane RP², while a polarity-sensitive control read by the same eyes and neurons gives a sphere. MAG-S3 adds what a real recording brings: the yield pattern of Ren et al. (2021), a modulation depth of the firing rate set directly from 10% to 100%, Poisson spikes, drift of the base rates, gain noise shared by the cells of a session, field rotations no faster than 100 µT/s, simultaneous recordings and pseudo-populations pooled from probe sessions of 80 cells and tetrode sessions of 6 cells, and a share of tuned cells of 1 or 0.1 with cell selection. The same recordings are read by an antipodal test of parity and by the frozen MAG-S2 topology pipeline gated by an atlas of synthetic shapes. The protocol (v0.4, in Russian), code and thresholds were frozen before the confirmatory run, and their SHA-256 were posted in Telegram (https://t.me/attractordm/76) at 18:28 UTC, before the run started at 18:28:57 UTC. In the confirmatory run (7 November 2026; maps on 10 virtual birds per cell, hypotheses on 100 new virtual birds) the input checks and all invariants passed, all four expectations and four of five hypotheses were met. The realistic pattern kept the RP² label in 82 of 100 birds and the polar control gave a sphere in 100 of 100. The polar control and shuffled data never got the RP² label, in 200 readouts of the second stage and 1500 of the maps. At a modulation depth of 40% the antipodal test called the code even in 100 of 100 birds with 100 cells, half of what topology needed, and it found an odd admixture at a level 20 times below the one at which topology gave a sphere. The hypothesis that pseudo-populations suffer less from shared gain noise than simultaneous recording failed in the opposite direction (RP² in 44 of 100 birds for simultaneous recording and in none for three probe sessions); an exploratory check after the run traces this to the gain noise of each session taking up principal components of its own, and dividing each presentation by the summed count of its session restored RP² in all ten birds checked. The maps give the requirements of an experiment: at a modulation depth of 40% or more, parity is seen with 6–12 cells in one session of about 44 minutes, while the shape needs 100–200 cells and several hours; with one tuned cell in ten, the shape fits none of the three recording budgets fixed before the run and the parity test fits all three. The release holds the frozen protocol and the protocol with its results, the code with its synthetic tests, the Colab notebook of the run, the archive of the confirmatory run with its verdicts, the calibration records, the checks before the run and the exploratory check.
